S01.name: Product Surfaces & Application Shell
S01.why: Headless MCP server. S01 is the human application frame (navigation, shell, empty/loading states); there is no such surface. The interaction contract lives in the MCP tool/resource surface and is judged under S08/S17 and B1.

S06.name: Domain Model Foundation
S06.why: inbox/models.py defines RevealRequest and IntegrationEvent as explicit state machines; delivery/normalize.py gives a vendor-neutral profile shape. Pydantic throughout. 17 tests in test_inbox.py exercise the transitions.

S08.name: Application / API Service Layer
S08.why: server.py create_server() is the single composition root; tools.py registers 10 MCP tools; routes.py serves /signalhire/callback/{tenant} and /health; resources.py serves resources. Covered by test_server.py (25) and test_tools.py (17). The scanner reported NONE — it looks for HTTP frameworks and misses an MCP surface.

S09.name: Database & Persistence
S09.why: Durable persistence moves to StaffHive/Supabase per ADR-0001 option A. This repo becomes stateless. InboxStore remains the reference implementation for staffhive#188's webhook_events state machine, but is retired here (W001-02).

S15.name: Event & Webhook Architecture
S15.why: Webhook RECEIPT moves to StaffHive per ADR-0001. This repo no longer terminates vendor webhooks. Was complete and correct; retired by an ownership decision, not by a defect.

S16.name: Integration Framework
S16.why: Delivery adapters (WebhookAdapter, McpAdapter) retired here per ADR-0001 option A -- StaffHive persists canonically and runs its own targeted CATS sync via the CATS MCP adapter (staffhive#187). Design preserved in the ADR.

S17.name: Public API / Developer Platform
S17.why: The MCP surface is the developer product and it is unusually well documented in place: server INSTRUCTIONS explain the credit model and the two-pool 402 trap, and bundled skills are served as MCP resources so a client learns the workflow without a local install. GAP: no versioned contract, no published schema, no changelog, no release — consumers cannot pin or detect a breaking change.

S38.name: Security
S38.why: pip-audit now runs on every push, watching the fastmcp 4.0.0b2 prerelease surface. Overbroad *credential* gitignore rule corrected -- it had excluded the credentials source package from the repo entirely. STILL PARTIAL: no SAST, and no PII retention policy for the durable inbox.

S40.name: Reliability & Resilience
S40.why: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter in the client honouring Retry-After; worker backoff capped at max_backoff_seconds; max_delivery_attempts then parks the event rather than dropping it, requeueable by hand; store recovers stuck events at startup; persist-before-ack. The failure modes were reasoned about explicitly.

S41.name: Observability
S41.why: logging_setup.py gives structured stderr logging with correlation IDs and a run_id filter; observability.py adds TimingMiddleware and documents at length why caching, rate limiting and response limiting are deliberately absent; /health reports inbox backlog and worker state rather than a bare 200. GAP: no metrics export, no tracing (FastMCP's OTel support is not wired), no alerting on the parked-event count.

S42.name: Infrastructure & Runtime Platform
S42.why: fastmcp.json declares the runtime, entrypoint and transport, and its interpolation traps are documented in place. Provider is now DECIDED: FastMCP Cloud (Prefect Horizon), which builds from the GitHub repo and reads requirements.txt/pyproject -- both present. GAP: no declared durable storage for data_dir (W001-02), and deploy-to-droplet.sh remains as a superseded parallel path that should be retired.

S43.name: Environments, CI/CD & Delivery
S43.why: CI is real and green as of W001-01: ci.yml runs pytest + ruff on 3.10/3.13, uv sync --frozen, and pip-audit on the exported lock, triggered on push/PR including staging/**. First passing run in repo history. STILL PARTIAL: no staging environment (W001-03), no release path (W001-04), promotion is still local -> production.

S44.name: Testing & Quality Architecture
S44.why: 86 tests pass and now gate every push and PR on two Python versions. ruff enforced. The suite was entirely dead until tests/__init__.py resolved the caio namespace shadow.

S45.name: Releases & Versioning
S45.why: pyproject and __init__ both declare 2.0.0, but there are zero git tags, zero GitHub releases, no CHANGELOG and no release workflow. Nothing records what 2.0.0 contains or how it differs from what a consumer already installed.
